newsitem.title: USA: ClinTrials sees Q2 loss of $0.08/shr.
newsitem.headline: ClinTrials sees Q2 loss of $0.08/shr.

text.p: ClinTrials Research Inc, which provides contract research to pharmaceutical companies, on Wednesday said it expected to report a second-quarter loss of $0.08 a share after some projects were cancelled.

"In the second quarter, we expect a modest loss," Chief Executive Officer William O'Neil told Reuters after a presentation to a Piper Jaffray investment conference here. "I wouldn't argue with an eight cent number," referring to the loss per share estimate.
In April, ClinTrials said it expected to report a loss in the second quarter as a result of contract cancellations. In the year-ago second quarter, ClinTrials earned $0.09 a share.

For the full year, O'Neil said he expected the Nashville, Tenn.-based company to report a profit equal to $0.05 a share. "That's what we are shooting to do," O'Neil said. "I think our prospects for hitting that are pretty good."
In 1996, the company earned $0.43 a share.
O'Neil he expected the company to rebuild its project backlog by the end of 1997.

"We expect improvements starting to show in the third quarter," O'Neil said. "Hopefully, by the end of the fourth quarter, we'll be back to a more normal track with our backlog rebuilt up north of $130 million. It's currently $102 million."
